The wax held the strips of paper on the board, and I would crop, edit, and arrange each to create the layout of the page. Many times, the blocks of text that made up an article were too long to fit within the space provided by a page's layout. In these cases, I would call an editor over so they could scan the article and use a pencil to draw red lines across the sections of text I should remove to make it fit within the available space. That is, the editor would mark up the text to indicate their intentions. In the digital era, we have markup languages like XML and HTML that use specific syntax to indicate the structure and formatting of text in the documents created with these languages.
